en: Dependent on a faulty (akusala) inferior state, a non-faulty non-inferior state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are three; under predominance condition there are three ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are three.

Dependent on an indeterminate (abyākata) intermediate state, a non-indeterminate non-intermediate state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Under root condition there are six; under object condition there are six ... pe ... under repetition condition there are five ... pe ... under result condition there are three ... pe ... under non-disappearance condition there are six.

Dependent on a wholesome, sublime state, an unwholesome, non-sublime state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. There are six in the case of root; six in the case of predominance … pe … three in the case of result … pe … six in the case of non-disappearance.
